newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends down in thin Christmas trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends down in thin Christmas trade.

text.p: Rubber futures closed slightly easier on Monday in extremely thin pre-Christmas trade with the market seen very quiet tomorrow ahead of the holiday on Wednesday, dealers said.
"We did absolutely nothing today. It's going to be very, very quiet tomorrow with the shortened trading day," a trader said.
The rubber futures market will end trading at 12 noon local time (0400 GMT), but most dealers said their offices will be closed anyway on Tuesday.
"We're closed tomorrow. See you after Christmas," another trader said. The market will reopen on Thursday.
Total volume traded for RSS3, RSS1 and TSR20 rubber reached only 300 tonnes each. The only contracts traded were the April/June RSS3 and RSS1 contract and the TSR20 February contract.
At around 0945 GMT, April/June RSS3 was seen at 129.50-130.50 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 130.75 cents.
April/June RSS1 was seen at 183.00-184.00 Singapore cents (US$1.30-$1.31) a kg from the previous 184.25 cents.
